text.p: Investors should hold shares of Polish cement firm Gorazdze SA, 51-percent controlled by CBR, as 1997 earnings should increase after last year's harsh winter, Flemings Research in London said in a report.

"Gorazdze's 1997 earnings outlook is positive, largely reflecting the sharp year on year recovery in the construction sector, from a mild 1997 winter following the harsh winter of 1996," the report said.

The report said net profits would rise to about 60 million zlotys this year and 64 million next year from 55.7 million in 1996 and sales would rise to 254 million zlotys this year and 282 million next year from 229 million in 1996.

Flemings said that while there was strong demand on the Polish market for cement, the firm's earnings were hampered by pressure on prices, capacity constraints and shrinking exports due to decreasing demand from Germany.
Gorazdze, Poland's largest cement plant, produced around 1.8 million tonnes of cement in 1996, with little scope for an increase in 1997 the report said.
